subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK questions
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-02-25T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo today — really useful overview. Quick recap of what we covered and the main pain points on our side:

- Latency spikes on synchronous generation during peak traffic (tail latency up to 15–30s) — streaming and lower tail latencies are a must
- High per-token cost for customer-facing features; want options to reduce unit cost (quantization, batching, embeddings + reranking)
- Need robust function calling / structured outputs for downstream systems (orders, service tickets)
- SDK integration must be lightweight — our stack is Node (public APIs) + Python backend; non-breaking changes are critical

Next steps we need from Redwood:
1) SDK change log and migration notes
2) High-level quote for three cluster sizes and sample SLA
3) SOC 2 evidence and answers to the security questionnaire for procurement
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with our engineering team (ideally next week)

I attached our requirements workbook for reference. Procurement will be on the thread when we get the security/quote items.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Account Executive
Acme Corp
Attachment: requirements.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-25T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK questions

Hi Alex — great to meet the team today. Recap below and proposed next steps so we're aligned.

Summary of goals / pain we heard:
- Reduce tail latency and enable streaming for end-user UX
- Lower unit cost with batching/quantization and use of embeddings + reranking for candidate selection
- Provide deterministic structured outputs via function calling to eliminate brittle downstream parsing
- Minimal SDK churn for your Node/Python stack; provide migration path

What we'll deliver this week:
- Redwoods SDK change log + migration notes (attached) — covers breaking changes, new streaming APIs, and function-calling examples
- Draft quote for three committed cluster sizes + example SLA by Friday
- Rishi will own security docs (SOC 2 + questionnaire) and will reply on this thread with evidence 
- Schedule: please share 2 windows next week for a 60-min deep-dive; Rishi and David will join for technical Q&A

Technical notes for the deep-dive (so your team can prep):
- We'll demo streaming token-level output and function calling with structured JSON responses
- Show embedding + reranking flow (generation -> embeddings -> vector search -> rerank) to reduce expensive decode calls
- Discuss quantization options and expected throughput impact on our Dedicated offering

Attaching: redwood_sdk_change_log.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_sdk_change_log.pdf

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2027-02-25T17:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK questions

Thanks Marissa — this is great. A couple quick clarifications from procurement: can you include an itemized pricing sheet in the quote (monthly committed + burst rates) and estimated cost for the embedding/reranking flow? Also, procurement wants to see SOC 2 type II evidence and a completed security questionnaire (I attached a blank questionnaire).

I'll propose two times for the technical deep-dive once I confirm with the engineering leads.

Alex
Attachment: procurement_questionnaire_blank.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-02-26T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK questions

Alex — thanks, looping next steps into action.

1) Attached is an initial quote (quote_v2.pdf) with itemized committed and burst pricing and a separate estimate for embedding + reranking throughput. This is a draft — we can refine after the tech deep-dive.
2) Rishi (cc'd) will follow up with SOC 2 Type II evidence and the completed security questionnaire by EOD tomorrow. He'll also coordinate the technical deep-dive scheduling with your engineering contacts.
3) We'll include a short appendix in the quote that outlines the streaming API, function-calling examples, and structured output contracts to make the engineering handoff smoother.

Proposed next meeting: Tue 2027-03-02 at 10:00am PT — does that work for your team?
